The Care Gaps Review Checklist

What to gather, compare and ask about the help Dad actually gets.

Download PDF

Dad has a care plan, an agency on the calendar and a sister who fills in. Before anyone says something is missing, make sure you have these in hand. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is a job for this week, not a finding about Dad's care.

Gather

Compare

Ask

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you gather, compare and ask. It doesn't tell you whether Dad's care is working or whether anything should change. A line marked “not sure” is something to check, and what the finished list means is for the people who assess him, and for the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You've pulled the papers together and lined up what Dad needs against the help in place. The care interview goes through his situation area by area, so that comparison rests on a whole picture and not on memory, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from

The item marked 1 uses the four areas of help the Family Caregiver Alliance lists. The items marked 2 follow the National Institute on Aging's advice to check in with the older person and the other caregivers. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. Family Caregiver Alliance, Hiring In-Home Help
  2. National Institute on Aging, Sharing Caregiving Responsibilities
